sources.name: Robinson et al. human RTK classification

notes: Inventory entries classify loci. Signaling coverage is established separately by the evidence graph.
GPCRdb data are adapted under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). This inventory keeps human protein-coding entries, strips display markup, and normalizes symbols to HGNC.

HGNC sensory loci without separate GPCRdb entries in the snapshot: OPN1MW2, OPN1MW3, OR1R1, OR2A42, OR2B8, OR2I1, OR4F16, OR4F29, OR51C1, OR56B2, OR5BS1, OR5D3, OR8G3, OR9H1, RGR, TAS2R2, TAS2R33, TAS2R36. HGNC classifies RGR as an opsin, and its listing does not imply demonstrated G-protein signaling.

GPCRdb entries excluded because HGNC does not classify the human locus as protein-coding: ADGRE4P, ADGRF2P, NPY6RP, TAAR3P, VN1R3. HGNC classifies TAS2R2 and VN1R5 as protein-coding with gene/pseudogene annotations.

The canonical RTK roster includes atypical or pseudokinase family members such as ERBB3, EPHA10, EPHB6, PTK7, ROR1, ROR2, RYK, and STYK1. FGFRL1 lacks the intracellular kinase domain and falls outside this roster.

Source SHA-256 digests for GPCRdb class responses concatenated in importer order and for HGNC TSV, respectively: 90d1036c200a315964032e4c1da23a77a0ee4d869cf6549dd8f38698db6c945e and 86cc190fcae1abcd77a13ddba9a34327150477f4e3c6bcadd7f445b26dd31246.
